newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica records another record trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica records another record trade deficit.

text.p: Jamaica's Statistical Institute reported Monday that the country recorded its third record trade deficit in just four years in 1996, with imports reaching twice the total value of exports.

Exports last year stood at US$1.4 billion, down four percent, while imports reached US$2.9 billion, up 2.6 percent, pushing the trade deficit to a record US$1.5 billion, up 10 percent over 1995's record.
Raw materials accounted for US$1.6 billion, or 55 percent of the total import bill. But that figure was a decline of US$22.3 million from 1995.
On the export side, non-traditional exports, including garments, fell 9.9 percent, while bauxite and alumina dipped 3.4 percent. Garments and bauxite/alumina are Jamaica's two largest export earners.
